designerWords:
Tony — the scene you want is already on the stage: "Double Slit (Tunnel, symmetric)", `dse-tunnel-rebuild`, loaded in its 3d mode, a 600 x 400 x 600 world. So nothing needs loading; one part moves.

How I read your words, so you can correct me after you have watched it: "farther from the slit wall" I take as farther along the beam, +40 px in x, away from the slits — not farther in depth. The slit wall's back face is at x 160 and the plate's front face is at x 315, so the leg from wall to plate is 155 px today; +40 makes it 195. The plate's centre goes from [325, 200, 0] to [365, 200, 0]: y stays on the beam axis, z stays 0, so the plate keeps its whole z -77..77 span inside the two invisible z-collimators and still sits well short of the far sink at x 590.

The parts, and the anchor. The anchor is the slit wall — the three red barrier segments and the two blue tunnels at x 96..160 — because that 155 px leg is measured from its back face and everything in this sketch is placed off it. Against that anchor: the source at [20, 200, 0] (unmoved), the start wall at the left edge (unmoved), slit1_channel at centre y 149 and slit2_channel at centre y 251 (unmoved), the far sink at x 590 (unmoved), and the one part that moves, `screen` — the GraphingDetectorWall that paints its own hit map on its own face — from centre [325, 200, 0] to [365, 200, 0].

Why that number matters, and where I am drawing it from. The sketch in `dse-tunnel-rebuild-build.md` does not pick 155 freely: it derives the leg from the ring ladder, D = sqrt(r₂² − halfSep²) with r₂ = 163.2 px and halfSep = 51, so that ring m = 2 of *both* slits crosses the axis exactly at the plate and the centre is doubly reinforced. Move the plate out to 195 and the axis point sits at radius sqrt(195² + 51²) ≈ 202 px from each slit exit — past ring 2 (163) and short of ring 3 (226). So this is a real counterfactual, not a cosmetic nudge: it takes the centre of the plate off a named ring. That is arithmetic from the sketch's own formula, not something I have watched.

The loop I am asking the Builder for: read inventory for the plate's live rect, film the scene as it stands, then drag the plate — one part, one axis, over ticks, inside a recording, so you watch it travel — and film it again long enough for the heat map to accumulate. One change only; nothing else in the scene is touched.

A caution on what the clip can show. `dse-tunnel-rebuild-seen.md` records that in the earlier clips the bands were not readable by 1502 ticks and were clear on the tile still at 7200. So I expect the after-clip to show dots arriving and the plate's map beginning to fill, and I would not promise crisp bands inside one clip. If the map reads as faint, the honest next step is a second, later clip of the same plate, not a second change.

builderWords:
I opened all eight sampled frames (frame-00, 08, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56) of DRAG screen — ticks 55709–56009.

**The result first.** `dragged: "screen"`, `from.center [325, 200, 0]` → `to.center [365, 200, 0]`, rect [315, 0, -77, 20, 400, 154] → [355, 0, -77, 20, 400, 154], zHeld false, 150 ticks of travel + 150 of settle, 61 frames, 6.1 s. That is the plan's change, and the plate ends at the plan's position.

**What the footage shows.** The side-on view: the start wall edge-on at the far left; the dense source-side dot cloud; the slit wall as three red blocks with bright blue channel bands and two open slots between them; a dark band; the detector panel with its coloured bin map; the far sink as a dark outlined panel at the right.

The plate travels, and this time it travels the way the outline asked. In frame-00 the panel sits close to the slab row with only a narrow dark band between them. Through frames 08, 16, 24 it walks steadily **right**, away from the slab row; by frames 40–56 it has stopped, and the dark band between the blocks and the panel is distinctly wider — I read it on screen as opening from roughly 40 px to roughly 65 px, with the panel's left edge moving about 25 px right. The panel also becomes slightly smaller in frame as it goes, as a thing receding from the eye does; the eye on this pose sits upstream, near x 0. The gap toward the far sink on the right narrows by the same amount. Everything else is fixed: start wall, blocks, channels, far sink, horizon.

**Dots cross the widened band in every frame.** They are sparser than the source-side cloud, scattered the whole way across, and still arriving at the panel's face at the end of the clip when the band is at its widest.

The map: the two warm cores at mid-height are there at the start and still there at the end, and over the second half of the clip they read a little smaller and a little less saturated to me, with more of the cyan-green field around them — the gentle reverse of the intensifying I watched on the inbound drag. The two dark blue columns persist throughout. I am reporting appearance, not cause: I have not tested whether that is the longer leg thinning the arrivals, the bins re-filling, or the colour scale moving, and a 6 s clip of a move cannot separate them.

**Against my PREDICTION.** Matched, and this time including the number: direction right and away from the slab row; the band widening; about 25 screen pixels of travel, which is what I predicted after calibrating on the previous clip rather than from my first arithmetic; the panel shrinking as it recedes; dots still crossing; the fixed slab row and far sink as references; the from/to in the result; and no countable fringes in 6 s. I also said I would watch the map rather than assert it stays put — and what I saw was a modest cooling, which I would not have predicted correctly had I committed to one.

**The build as it now stands, against the plan and against the Owl's one change.**
- Scene `dse-tunnel-rebuild`, mode `3d`, untouched; no part added, removed, resized or re-declared.
- The plan's one change is in place and filmed: `screen` from centre [325, 200, 0] to [365, 200, 0], the leg from the slit wall's back face (x 160) 155 → 195 px, y and depth untouched (z span still -77..77).
- The Owl's one change is in place: camera azimuth -150, elevation -12, roll 0, distance 470, target (230, 200, 0), so the wall-to-screen axis runs across the frame. A fresh `inventory` reading confirms both: `screen` centre [365, 200, 0], rect [355, 0, -77, 20, 400, 154]; camera as set; `viewer.toward` now `-z`, consistent with the eye sitting on the -z side as I derived.
- The re-staging is on the record and labelled: to produce a before-and-after under one camera I dragged the plate back to [325, 200, 0] (filmed, turn 10) and then forward again to [365, 200, 0] (filmed, this turn). Nothing is presented as the original drag, and the scene ends where the plan puts it.
- No hand was refused. The only parts out of reach are `zClipNear` and `zClipFar`, declared in the scene's code; the plan never asked for them.

**What I got wrong along the way, kept in the record rather than tidied away:** the first camera made the asked-for move unreadable and I handed that clip on anyway; I claimed dots crossing the gap from footage that could not show it; I claimed a halo broadening that the pixels did not support; I offered a scale ruler that this camera's obliquity invalidates; and my first screen-displacement estimate was 35 px against an actual ~25.

The judgement is the Owl's, not mine. What the last clip shows is the plate moving 40 px farther from the slit wall, across the frame, with the gap widening, particles crossing it, and the pattern on its face still forming.

owl.words:
# Owl — turn 12 (thread mmt41a-owl-r2)

All 8 frames opened, in order: frame-00, 08, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56. Every claim below is read off those
pixels. I did not plan and did not build this; I judge the footage against the outline and the prediction only.

## ACCOUNT — what the pixels show

**The parts in the block, left to right.** A thin vertical white wireframe strip at the far left (x≈40–80),
full frame height. A stack of three red slabs with pale-blue caps (the slit wall) at x≈150–285, with two
gaps between the caps — the upper gap at y≈150–165, the lower at y≈250–265. A tall panel with a cyan/green
rim carrying a heatmap face, starting at x≈325. A far dark wireframe panel with an almost empty black face
at x≈465–585. A dense cloud of small yellow dots fills the space between the left strip and the slab row,
with sparser dots to the right of the slabs.

**contact.** The dot cloud first meets the slit wall on its left face, in the **middle third** of the wall's
height — the dots funnel at the two slit gaps between the blue caps, and the blue caps themselves are
peppered with dots where the cloud lands on them (clearest on the middle and lower caps, frames 08–56).
The next part reached is the heatmap panel's left face: the two red/orange cores sit at y≈175–200 on a panel
spanning y≈8–368, i.e. the **middle third** vertically, straddling the panel's horizontal **middle** (x≈355
and x≈382 in frame-00, drifting right with the panel). The far dark wireframe panel is reached only by a few
isolated specks; its face is otherwise black in all 8 frames.

**after.** After the slits the dots go **straight on to the right**, across the dark gap toward the heatmap
panel — I count dots at x≈290–330 in every frame, including frame-56. Nothing turns back toward the source;
no upward or downward deflection is visible at the slits.

**passes.** **Yes, some passes the panel.** Faint specks sit in the gap beyond the heatmap panel and on the
far dark sink face — e.g. around (520, 95) and (480, 150) in frame-00, (475, 160) in frame-16, (540, 280) and
(475, 300) in frames 48 and 56. Dots also pass **above and below** the slab stack instead of through the
slits (cloud extends past y≈20 and y≈390 on the left side).

**The motion in the clip.** The heatmap panel's near (left) edge reads ≈325 (f-00), 328 (f-08), 335 (f-16),
340 (f-24), 345 (f-32), 348 (f-40), 350 (f-48), 352 (f-56); its far edge ≈418 → ≈440 over the same frames.
So the panel drifts **right, away from the slab row, by ~25–28 screen pixels**, monotonically. The dark gap
between the slab row's right edge (≈285, unmoving) and the panel's left edge widens from ≈40 px to ≈67 px.
The gap between the panel and the far dark sink narrows from ≈47 px to ≈28 px. The slab row and the far
sink hold their positions within my reading precision (±3 px); the left strip is fixed. The panel's apparent
face width narrows slightly, ≈93 px → ≈88 px, while its height is unchanged (≈8 to ≈366 throughout).

**The map.** The two red cores persist at the same mid-height in all 8 frames; they neither vanish nor
migrate. The central navy band reads somewhat darker and broader from frame-24 on. The face shows a broad
dark central band with cyan/green flanks and the two warm cores — **no countable fringe train** in the clip.

## Judging the OUTLINE, part by part

- *the 3D double slit* — present: source cloud, a slit wall with **two** gaps, a detector panel carrying the
  map, and the far sink. ✔
- *the detector screen moved farther from the slit wall* — present and it is the **only** thing that moves:
  the heatmap panel travels right, away from the slabs, and the widening dark band (40→67 px) is the
  separation growing. ✔
- *by 40 pixels* — I cannot read world units off pixels; what the pixels show is a move of the right
  **sense** (away from the wall) and of a screen size (~25 px) consistent with a 40-unit world step under
  this perspective. Nothing in the frames contradicts it. ✔
- Nothing else in the outline is asked and nothing extra moves — the slit wall, the left strip and the far
  sink are fixed. ✔

## Judging the PREDICTION, item by item

- "panel slides RIGHT across the frame, away from the slab row, by about 25 screen pixels" — **matches**:
  ~25–28 px, monotonic, measured edge by edge.
- "the dark band between the slabs and the panel widens correspondingly" — **matches**: ≈40 → ≈67 px.
- "against the same fixed slab row and far sink" — **matches**: both hold position.
- "the panel shrinks slightly as it recedes" — **weakly supported**: face width narrows ≈5 px, height
  unchanged. Not contradicted, but it is at the edge of what I can resolve, so I do not confirm it strongly.
- "dots keep crossing the widened band" — **matches**: dots at x≈290–330 in every frame, frame-56 included.
- "the warm cores may cool or spread… I am watching for that rather than asserting it" — hedged, so nothing
  to contradict; the pixels show the cores **holding** at the same mid-height through frame-56.
- "no countable fringes in 6 s" — **matches**: a broad dark band and two cores, no countable fringes.

No account item disagrees with the outline: no wrong third, no wrong direction, no part the outline has the
stream meet that it instead sails past. The one thing the beam does do beyond the outline — a few specks
reaching the far sink — is the sink doing its job, not a missing part. **Approve.**
